summary: SEC-001 Rooms, SEC-002 Event creation, and SEC-003 like/RSVP/leaderboard authorization fixes VERIFIED against the live preview (https://circles-demo-1.preview.emergentagent.com) — 34/34 pytest cases green. Specifically closed: (SEC-002) POST /circles/{id}/events — owner/member 200, non-member 403, non-existent circle 404; (SEC-001) rooms tied to a PRIVATE circle — guide owner 200 on GET /rooms/{id}, GET /rooms/{id}/messages and POST /rooms/{id}/messages; non-member 403 on GET /rooms/{id}, POST /rooms/{id}/join, GET /rooms/{id}/messages, POST /rooms/{id}/messages; create_room with circle_id user isn't a member of → 403; create_room with unknown circle_id → 404; global rooms (no circle_id) remain OPEN — non-member can GET/join/post/read. (SEC-003) POST /posts/{postId}/like — non-member of private circle 403, member 200, non-existent post 404; POST /events/{eventId}/rsvp — non-member 403, member 200, non-existent event 404; GET /circles/{id}/leaderboard — non-member 403 for private, member 200, non-existent 404. Regression confirmed: PUBLIC-circle member can create event/RSVP/like/leaderboard (all 200), public leaderboard also readable by non-member (public circles stay open for reads), GET /rooms list works for non-members, guide can create+join+message its own global rooms. Prior-fix regression also holds: non-member posting into private circle 403, DM IDOR (non-participant → GET /conversations/{id}/messages) 403, self-gift POST /gifts 400, under-13 /auth/register 403.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2017 lines — strongly recommend splitting into routers (auth, circles, posts, rooms, events, conv, wallet, moderation, compliance). Carried over from iter9.

assert_can_access_room() silently no-ops if room.circle_id is set but the circle no longer exists (orphan room). Low risk — only reachable if admin deletes a circle but not its rooms — but worth either 404'ing the orphan room or deleting rooms on circle delete.

toggle_like() and toggle_rsvp() both wrap assert_can_read_circle() in `if pc:` / `if ec:` branches, meaning a like/rsvp on content whose parent circle was deleted bypasses the guard. Same orphan-safety nit as rooms. Consider 404 on missing parent circle.

create_event correctly 404s on unknown circle_id and relies on assert_can_write (which chains is_member + ban/mute checks). create_room matches the pattern with its own in-line is_member call — minor code-duplication, could reuse a single helper.
No new bugs found — SEC-001/002/003 fixes are correctly implemented on live preview.
